claims.statement: In the legacy SimpleWay Taijifu manifesto, Taijifu is described as the physical and martial system.
In the legacy SimpleWay Taijifu manifesto, SimpleWay Taijifu is described as the teaching, practice, and evolution layer of Taijifu.
The legacy SimpleWay Taijifu manifesto names a central progression sequence: learn fundamentals, practice, measure, correct, and advance.
The legacy SimpleWay Taijifu manifesto states that its curriculum arises from real practice and progressive validation rather than remaining only theoretical.
The legacy SimpleWay Taijifu principles prioritize technique before power, control before speed, stability before complexity, progression before intensity, and precision before volume.
The legacy SimpleWay Taijifu principles treat recovery as part of training and require evolution to be measurable and training to be adaptable to the practitioner.
The legacy SimpleWay Taijifu principles state that physical conditioning and technique are integrated progressively and that safety takes priority over completing a training session.
TAIJIFU é Arte Marcial de se Adaptar.
TAI expresses essência/permanência/Axis and asks what must remain.
JI expresses discernimento/adaptação/Nexus and asks what needs to change.
FU expresses manifestação/fluxo/Flow and asks what form must exist now.
Firme na essência. Livre na forma.
HNK nasce do AMOR e torna-se ferramenta/manifestação do AMOR; TAIJIFU trabalha o tornar-se e a adaptação sem abandono da essência.

reconciliation.reason: Current authority defines Taijifu more broadly as an art of adaptation; it does not explicitly confirm the legacy physical-and-martial-system-only formulation.
PHIL-SRC-0004 does not define SimpleWay Taijifu's product-layer relationship.
The TAI/JI/FU cycle is compatible with progression and change but does not explicitly canonize the legacy learning sequence.
Current authority does not address curriculum construction or progressive validation.
The current maxims support preservation of essence with adaptable form but do not explicitly canonize these five training priorities.
Adaptation is current Canon, while recovery and measurable evolution are not addressed by PHIL-SRC-0004.
Current authority does not address conditioning integration or training-session safety.
